blocked.blockedOn: Gate G3 skips because UNITY_LICENSE and the GameCI secrets are absent, so Unity-side code cannot be shown to compile or pass. This is why WO-0007 was correctly scoped to Core and Tests only, and why PRO-0001 is filed rather than folded into WO-0007.

notes:
PLACEMENT RULING (WO-0007, run identity: Seed and TickCount). Both belong in Assets/Core, on RunState itself. Run identity is not a rendering or platform concern; it is the coordinate that makes a run replayable, and a coordinate is only worth anything if it is attached to the state it describes. ADR-0001 makes reproducibility from a seed the entire justification for Core being engine-free, so putting the seed in the Unity shell would leave Core -- the three quarters of the game that is actually verifiable without a licence -- unable to name the run it is simulating, and would make every headless balance run anonymous. TickCount is the same argument in the time dimension: it must be a direct count of Tick calls, incremented in Core, because a shell-side frame counter would be a different number on every machine and would reintroduce exactly the wall-clock coupling that taking dt as a parameter was designed to remove. Neither field needs UnityEngine, neither reads an ambient clock, and neither draws on an unseeded source, so the purity check is unaffected. The shell's legitimate share of this is only choosing which seed to pass and displaying the pair, which is adapter work and is the subject of PRO-0001. Ruling: Core, and the Core/Unity boundary is not moved by this order.

ASSESSMENT OF CRITERION 10. It is satisfiable as written, and I am not challenging it. The concern it invites -- that a parameterless constructor forces a default seed which hides non-determinism -- is already closed by criterion 9, which requires that any unsupplied seed be a fixed documented constant and forbids wall-clock time, static counters and every other unseeded source. A fixed constant default is fully deterministic; it is less varied than a chosen seed, not less reproducible, and 'less varied' is the safe direction for a replay coordinate. The two criteria are therefore consistent, and the honest implementation is a public parameterless constructor chaining to the seeded one with a public documented constant, which also keeps the existing tests in Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/RunStateTests.cs (which all call `new RunState()`) compiling. The genuine cost of criterion 10 is downstream and outside this order: it lets the Unity shell keep constructing runs without ever stating a seed, so the seed WO-0007 adds will never vary or be visible where a human plays. That is a shell defect, not a Core one, and I have raised it as PRO-0001 rather than widening WO-0007's write scope to Assets/Unity, which I have no authority to do and which G3 could not verify in any case. I would resist only one reading of criterion 10: if it were ever taken to mean the parameterless constructor is the primary or encouraged path, that would be wrong. It is a compatibility shim for one existing call site, and the seeded constructor is the real API.

DESIGN NOTE TO THE IMPLEMENTER (non-binding where the criteria are silent). Criterion 1 does not name the seed's type; uint is the recommendation, because it matches XorShiftRng's constructor exactly and lets a run's seed be handed to the RNG with no conversion or range question, and because criterion 1's demand that every representable value including zero survive unchanged is cleanest over an unsigned type. Criterion 1 also draws the right distinction and it must be honoured: XorShiftRng remaps seed 0 because a zero xorshift state is a fixed point, which is an algorithm constraint; RunState.Seed is an identity and must return zero if zero was given. Do not copy the remap. TickCount should be an int or long field incremented in Tick after the IsOver early-return and after the dt validation throw, never computed from ElapsedSeconds, whose float accumulation is exactly the lossy path criterion 3 is written to forbid.

ALLOCATION. WO-0007 is allocated to core-simulation-engineer, unchanged from the order's named agent, single owner, no split. It is one file of production code and its tests, and splitting it would cost more in coordination than it saves. Quality's independent verification and the G2 verdict sit outside this division by design. Write scope stays Assets/Core/Run/** and Assets/Tests/Core.Tests/** as the order states; the two escalateIf conditions in WO-0007 come to me first, and my expectation is that neither fires, since the parameterless constructor is preservable without touching Assets/Unity and a Seed plus a TickCount is sufficient identity without persisting full IRng state. No other work orders were open to this division this period.

BOUNDARIES OBSERVED. I wrote no production code and no test code; Assets/** is untouched by me. I did not amend WO-0007's acceptance criteria, including criterion 10 which I was invited to scrutinise; assessing a criterion and editing it are different acts and only the first is mine. I marked nothing complete -- completed is empty and WO-0007 is inFlight, because completion is a gate verdict and I may not gate my own division. I did not extend WO-0007 to Assets/Unity/GameManager.cs despite believing that file needs a change; that became PRO-0001. needsFounderAttention is empty because nothing here is founder-only: the design blocker is already carried in the executive humanQueue against WO-0002, and restating it as an escalation id that does not exist would inflate the queue rather than inform it.
